bugs.name: Open with editors misspells IntelliJ IDEA
bugs.summary: The site configuration list labels IntelliJ IDEA as “Intellij IDEA.”
bugs.expected: The editor name should use the product’s capitalization, IntelliJ IDEA.
bugs.actual: The site configuration list labels IntelliJ IDEA as “Intellij IDEA.”
reproSteps: Open Site Administration → Configuration → Settings.
Expand Open with editors and read the IntelliJ IDEA entry.

bugs.name: Cron task label contains duplicate punctuation
bugs.summary: The archive cleanup task ends with “etc..” in the Cron Tasks list.
bugs.expected: The task label should end with one period.
bugs.actual: The archive cleanup task ends with “etc..” in the Cron Tasks list.
reproSteps: Open Site Administration → Monitoring → Cron Tasks.
Find the Delete all repositories’ archives task and inspect its label.

bugs.name: Admin repository alphabetical sort groups results by owner
bugs.summary: The eval repository list places an organization’s aaa-org-repo after all eval-owned repositories when sorted Alphabetically.
bugs.expected: Alphabetically should order the Name column across owners.
bugs.actual: The eval repository list places an organization’s aaa-org-repo after all eval-owned repositories when sorted Alphabetically.
reproSteps: Create a disposable organization and an organization repository named aaa-org-repo alongside eval-owned repositories.
Open Site Administration → Code Assets → Repositories and choose Sort → Alphabetically.
Observe that aaa-org-repo appears after all eval-owned names, including names starting with m.

bugs.name: Malformed Open with editor override is silently discarded without validation feedback
bugs.summary: Submitting a nonempty Open with editor override without the required mapping delimiter silently clears the field without explaining that the entry was discarded.
bugs.expected: When a nonempty editor entry is discarded because its mapping is malformed, provide visible feedback explaining what needs correction. An intentionally empty override should continue to select the defaults.
bugs.actual: On two submissions, Malformed Editor Entry was visible before Save, but the settings page reloaded with a blank textarea and no validation message. Refreshing kept the field blank. The help gives mappings using = and explains that an empty override uses the defaults.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval, an administrator, on a disposable Gitea fixture. Open Site Administration > Configuration > Settings and start with the Repository Open with editor override empty.
Enter Malformed Editor Entry in the editor override textarea, omitting the = delimiter, and click that section’s Save button.
Observe that the page reloads with a blank textarea and no visible explanation that the nonempty entry was invalid and discarded.
Repeat the same nonempty entry and Save. Confirm the same silent clearing, then refresh and confirm the field remains blank.
Expand the help to see the mapped examples using = and the stated empty-field default behavior. Leave the override empty and save to restore the initial default configuration.
bugs.sourceCause: The settings parser skips nonempty lines that lack = or either mapping component without returning an error. With every line skipped, it saves a nil editor list successfully; the reloaded textarea is blank and the form receives no validation feedback.

bugs.name: Stacktrace page overflows mobile viewport
bugs.summary: At 390×844, the Stacktrace page permits whole-document horizontal scrolling that shifts the process card and controls offscreen.
bugs.expected: Horizontal scrolling for long stack text should remain within its content area and leave the process card and page controls in place.
bugs.actual: A normal horizontal scroll from the page margin outside the stack content shifts the process card and Download diagnosis report control left and exposes blank space. The document already overflows before expanding ProcessStacktraces.func2; expansion is part of the observed flow, not an established cause.
reproSteps: Sign in as a site administrator in the current Gitea fixture and set a desktop browser viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Use Site Administration → Monitoring → Trace → Stacktrace.
Locate the monitoring request process and expand code.gitea.io/gitea/modules/process.(*Manager).ProcessStacktraces.func2.
From the page margin outside the card/code content, perform a normal horizontal scroll to the right, approximately 350 CSS pixels.
Observe the process card and diagnosis controls shifting left and blank space appearing on the right. The overflow is already present before the expansion.

relatedReference.distinction: The existing reference concerns the diagnosis button covering the Stacktrace tab label. This reference concerns stack content causing whole-document horizontal displacement; toolbar overlap alone is not treated as its evidence.

bugs.name: At mobile width, the diagnosis-report button overlaps and obscures the Stacktrace tab label
bugs.summary: At mobile width, the diagnosis-report button overlaps and obscures the Stacktrace tab label
bugs.expected: The Stacktrace tab and Download diagnosis report button are separately laid out so the button does not obscure the tab label or its click target at this viewport.
bugs.actual: At 390 × 844, the Download diagnosis report button covers the right side of the Stacktrace tab, leaving its label partially hidden. The exposed part of the tab remains clickable.
reproSteps: /-/admin/monitor/stacktrace

Read-only browser exploration only. Do not change authentication details or sign out; do not create, start, stop, or modify running jobs or global data. Do not inspect application source, benchmarks, ground truth, or prior evaluation reports, and do not treat coverage metadata or failed/untested jobs as bugs.
Start with the authorized administrator session and navigate to /-/admin/monitor/stacktrace at a 390 × 844 CSS-pixel viewport.
Observe the toolbar above the goroutine count. The Download diagnosis report button overlaps the Stacktrace tab.

matchingGuidance.acceptanceScope: Accepted as a valid reference by user instruction; source prerequisites and remaining evidence gaps are retained below.
prerequisites: 390px content width below tab strip plus diagnosis form intrinsic widths.

bugs.name: Mobile organization total overlaps its create button
bugs.summary: At a 390px width, the New Organization button covers part of the organization-total heading.
bugs.expected: At mobile width, the organization heading and New Organization button should not paint over each other. Wrapping or deliberate truncation is acceptable; the defect is overlap.
bugs.actual: After returning to the inventory, the header visibly reads “Organization Management (Total: 8” and the New Organization button covers the closing parenthesis. The number 8 is legible, but the complete label is not; the overlap remains static in the recorded view.
reproSteps: Sign in as a site administrator, use English, and set the viewport to 390 by 844 CSS pixels.
Open Site Administration > Organizations and choose New Organization.
Create a uniquely named disposable public organization using the default permissions, then return through the UI to the administrator organization inventory.

Inspect Organization Management (Total: N) beside New Organization. In the supplied reproduction at Total: 8, the button covers the closing parenthesis. The numeric total stays readable and organization creation succeeds.

bugs.name: Deleting a repository clears administrator inventory search and privacy filters
bugs.summary: After an administrator deletes the sole repository matching an inventory search and Public filter, the redirect drops both query parameters, clears the search, and displays unrelated repositories instead of the now-empty filtered results.
bugs.expected: After successful deletion, return to the same inventory search and privacy filter. Since the deleted repository was the only match, show the filtered empty state rather than unrelated repositories.
bugs.actual: The session narrative reports that the administrator searched `qa-delete-filter`, selected Public (`private=0`), and confirmed deletion. It then landed at `/-/admin/repos?page=1&sort=recentupdate` without `q` or `private`, where unrelated `harbor-handbook` appeared.
reproSteps: As an administrator, have a disposable public repository named `qa-delete-filter` and another public repository `harbor-handbook`.
Open /-/admin/repos, search for `qa-delete-filter`, and select the Public filter. Confirm only the matching repository appears.
Click that repository's delete control and confirm deletion.
Observe whether the resulting inventory URL retains `q=qa-delete-filter` and `private=0`; the recorded session narrative says both are dropped and unrelated repositories are shown.

bugs.name: Deleting the last repository on page two strands the administrator on an empty page
bugs.summary: When an administrator deletes the only repository on the last page of Site Administration → Repositories, the redirect returns to that now out-of-range page, which shows the total count but "No results found." and no pagination controls.
bugs.expected: After deleting the last repository on a page, the administrator lands on a page that lists repositories, such as the new last page, or at least has pagination controls to get back.
bugs.actual: The delete redirects to /-/admin/repos?page=2&sort=oldest, which shows "Total: 50" with "No results found." and no pagination, so there is no in-page way back. Reloading repeats it. Deleting a repository that isn't alone on its page works normally.
reproSteps: Sign in as an administrator and make sure Site Administration → Repositories has exactly one repository more than a page holds (51 with the default page size of 50), creating disposable repositories if needed.
Open /-/admin/repos, sort by Oldest, and go to page 2, which lists only the newest repository.
Delete that repository and confirm.
Observe that the page stays at /-/admin/repos?page=2&sort=oldest showing "Total: 50" and "No results found." with no pagination controls.
As a control, delete a repository that shares its page with others and confirm the list still shows results.

bugs.name: Mobile user and repository inventory totals are covered by their action buttons
bugs.summary: At 390px the Site Administration User Accounts and Repositories headings are overlapped by their absolutely positioned action buttons, so Create User Account and Unadopted Repositories paint over the 'Total: N' count.
bugs.expected: The 'Total: N' count in the User Account Management and Repository Management headings stays readable beside the action button at mobile width, as it is on desktop.
bugs.actual: At 390×844, Create User Account covers the end of 'User Account Management (Total: N)' and Unadopted Repositories covers the end of 'Repository Management (Total: N)', hiding the number. The overlap persists after reload and after the totals change. From 480px up, and on desktop, both counts are fully readable. The buttons still work.
reproSteps: Sign in as an administrator and set the viewport to 390×844.
Open Site Administration → User Accounts and look at the heading total beside Create User Account.
Open Site Administration → Repositories and look at the heading total beside Unadopted Repositories.
Widen the viewport to 1280px and observe both totals are readable.

relatedReference.distinction: Both come from the same absolutely positioned header button overlapping the inventory heading at mobile width, but on different pages: this reference covers the User Accounts and Repositories inventories, and the related reference covers the Organizations inventory with New Organization. Credit each finding to the reference for the page it reports.

bugs.name: Organization Follow button label splits across lines at mobile width
bugs.summary: Below 768px on an organization’s profile, the Follow button is squeezed beside the organization name and its label breaks mid-word (“Fol”/“low”; “Unfollow” across three lines).
bugs.expected: At phone width the Follow/Unfollow button keeps its label on one line, or the header wraps so the button has room.
bugs.actual: At 390px on an organization page reached from Site Administration > Organizations, the Follow button shrank to about 62×46px and rendered “Fol” and “low” on two lines; after following, “Unfollow” split into “Unf”/“ollo”/“w”. Widths of 768px and up, and a one-letter display name, rendered on one line.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and set the viewport to 390×844.
Open Site Administration > Organizations and open an organization with a typical-length display name.
Look at the Follow button next to the organization name and observe its label split mid-word across lines.

bugs.name: Clearing an organization's Contact Email reports success but keeps the old address
bugs.summary: In organization settings, emptying the Contact Email field and clicking Update Settings shows 'Organization settings have been updated.', but the old address is kept in the form and the organization header.
bugs.expected: Saving an empty Contact Email removes the saved address, or shows a validation error if an address is required.
bugs.actual: After clearing orgs-qa@example.com and clicking Update Settings, the success banner appeared but the field and the organization header showed orgs-qa@example.com again, including after refresh.
reproSteps: Open an organization's settings and save a Contact Email.
Clear the Contact Email field and click Update Settings.
Check the banner, the field and the organization header, then refresh.

bugs.name: Clearing a user's repository limit in admin Edit User silently saves 0
bugs.summary: In Site Administration > Edit User, clearing the Maximum Number of Repositories field and saving reports success but stores 0, which blocks the user from creating any repositories, instead of rejecting the blank value or using the default (-1).
bugs.expected: A blank repository limit is rejected with a validation message, or falls back to the documented default (-1, the global limit); it doesn't silently become 0.
bugs.actual: With the limit at -1, clearing the field and clicking Update User Account showed 'The user account has been updated.'; reopening Edit showed Maximum Number of Repositories set to 0.
reproSteps: As a site administrator, open a user's Edit page in Site Administration (limit shows -1).
Clear the Maximum Number of Repositories field and click Update User Account.
Reopen Edit and read the limit.

bugs.name: Rejected organization rename discards the other unsaved organization settings edits
bugs.summary: In organization settings, submitting a name that's already taken or reserved shows the right error, but the form is redrawn from the saved values, so the other edits from the same submission (full name, description, website, location, visibility, repository limit) are lost.
bugs.expected: The rejected name is reported while the other entered values stay in the form, so the admin can fix the name and save without re-entering them.
bugs.actual: Renaming an organization to another organization's existing name, with a new full name 'Bravo unsaved validation draft' and description entered, showed 'The username is already taken.' but the full name and description reverted to blank and the name reverted to the old one.
reproSteps: Create two organizations.
Open the second organization's settings, set its name to the first organization's name, and change the full name and description.
Click Update Settings and check the fields after the error.

relatedReference.distinction: Same organization settings form. That entry is clearing Contact Email being ignored on a successful save; this entry is a rejected rename discarding the other unsaved edits.

bugs.name: Queue worker cap below -1 is silently saved as -1
bugs.summary: In Site Administration > Monitoring > Queues, entering a maximum worker count below -1 (such as -2) reports Settings Updated and stores -1 instead. The form gives no validation message or sign that the entered value was rejected or changed.
bugs.expected: An out-of-range worker cap is either rejected with a validation message or the page says the value was adjusted, instead of reporting success for a value that wasn't saved.
bugs.actual: For the repo-archive queue, entering -2 in Max Number of workers and clicking Update Settings showed Settings Updated, but the queue's maximum then showed -1, and it stayed -1 after a refresh. Nothing on the page mentioned the change.
reproSteps: As an administrator, open Site Administration > Monitoring > Queues and open a queue's worker settings.
Enter -2 as the maximum number of workers and click Update Settings.
Compare the saved maximum with the value entered, and check for any validation or adjustment message.

bugs.name: Cancelling a running diagnosis report leaves it running
bugs.summary: In Site Administration > Monitor, confirming Cancel on a running diagnosis report process reports success, but the process keeps running for its full duration and the browser still downloads the report afterwards. The diagnosis handler waits out its full time without checking for cancellation.
bugs.expected: Cancelling the diagnosis process stops it promptly, so it disappears from the process list and no report is downloaded.
bugs.actual: After confirming Cancel, the page reported success, but the diagnosis process stayed in the list for the rest of its run and the browser then downloaded the report as usual.
reproSteps: In Site Administration > Monitor, start a diagnosis report with a long duration (for example 90 seconds).
While it runs, find its process in the Monitor's process list and click Cancel, then confirm.
Watch whether the process disappears from the list and whether the report still downloads when the duration ends.

bugs.name: A rejected organization settings save unchecks 'Repository admins can change team access'
bugs.summary: When saving an organization's settings is rejected (for example a name that's already taken), the form reloads with the error, but the previously checked 'Repository admin can add and remove access for teams' option is unchecked. Fixing the error and saving again turns that permission off without the user noticing.
bugs.expected: A rejected organization settings save keeps every option as the user left it, including the team-access permission.
bugs.actual: Renaming an organization to a taken name showed 'The username is already taken.' and the team-access checkbox, previously checked, came back unchecked; saving again after fixing the name saved it as off.
reproSteps: In an organization's Settings, make sure 'Repository admin can add and remove access for teams' is checked and saved.
Change the organization name to one that's already taken and click Update Settings.
Check the team-access checkbox on the error page, then fix the name, save, and reload.

bugs.name: Admin User Accounts search and filters drop the selected sort
bugs.summary: In Site Administration > User Accounts, choosing a sort and then searching or applying a filter reloads the list in alphabetical order, dropping the selected sort.
bugs.expected: Searching or filtering User Accounts keeps the selected sort order.
bugs.actual: With reverse-alphabetical sort selected, searching or filtering returned the matching users in alphabetical order and the sort parameter was gone from the URL.
reproSteps: Open Site Administration > User Accounts and choose a non-default sort, such as reverse alphabetical.
Enter a search term (or change a filter) and submit.
Check the order of the results and the selected sort.

relatedReference.name: Admin Organizations search drops the selected sort
relatedReference.distinction: Same missing sort field in the search form, but that entry is the Organizations list; this entry is User Accounts.

bugs.name: Admin Organizations search drops the selected sort
bugs.summary: In Site Administration > Organizations, choosing a sort and then searching reloads the list in alphabetical order, dropping the selected sort.
bugs.expected: Searching Organizations keeps the selected sort order.
bugs.actual: With reverse-alphabetical sort selected, searching returned the matching organizations in alphabetical order and the sort parameter was gone from the URL.
reproSteps: Open Site Administration > Organizations and choose a non-default sort, such as reverse alphabetical.
Enter a search term and submit.
Check the order of the results and the selected sort.

relatedReference.name: Admin User Accounts search and filters drop the selected sort
relatedReference.distinction: Same missing sort field in the search form, but that entry is User Accounts; this entry is the Organizations list.

bugs.name: Out-of-range repository limit silently replaces the saved value with 0
bugs.summary: On Site Administration > Edit User Account, entering a Maximum Number of Repositories that's too large (or not a plain number, such as 1e3) shows "The user account has been updated" but saves the limit as 0, erasing the previous value and blocking the user from creating repositories.
bugs.expected: An invalid repository limit is rejected with an error and the saved limit is kept.
bugs.actual: With a saved limit of 7, entering 99999999999999999999999999999 and saving showed a success message; reopening the account showed the limit as 0.
reproSteps: In Site Administration, edit a user and set Maximum Number of Repositories to 7; save.
Change it to a very large number (or 1e3) and click Update User Account.
Reopen the user's Edit page and check the limit.

bugs.name: Browser Back restores repository results with the wrong visible search query
bugs.summary: After searching for a matching repository, submitting an unmatched query and going back, the earlier repository results return while the search field continues to display the unmatched query.
bugs.expected: The restored search field matches the restored results and prior search query.
bugs.actual: The table returns qa-repos-private-739 with Total: 1, while the visible search field still shows & # ' " %.
reproSteps: Open Site administration → Code Assets → Repositories.
Search a fresh prefix with matching records and confirm the results.
Submit another query with no matches.
Use Browser Back and observe the earlier matching results while the visible search input retains the newer query.
Reload the restored URL and confirm the input and results agree.

relatedReference.distinction: This entry covers admin Repositories search; the related entry covers admin Users search.

matchingGuidance.scope: Covers a visible retained newer query alongside correctly restored earlier results after Browser Back. Subsequent actions submitting the retained query are separate effects.

reviewEvidence.basis: Explicit user acceptance at severity 1 after coordinator corrected an overlooked Codex reproduction of admin repository management during case #9.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Contradictory visible search state; no incorrect saved records or data loss established.
analysis: Codex independently reproduced the visible query/results mismatch and explicitly lists admin repository management among observed affected callers.
The same review distinguished the live input value from its restored HTML default value and recommended severity 1.
User explicitly accepted both admin entry points.
limitations: The admin observation comes from the broader case #9 review; no separate case #22 judge run was completed.

bugs.name: Browser Back restores user results but leaves the later search text
bugs.summary: After searching mo-order- then missing-order-qa and navigating Back, the table returns the previous mo-order- results while the search input displays missing-order-qa.
bugs.expected: The search input restores the previous search query to match the displayed search results.
bugs.actual: The table displays the two mo-order users (Total: 2), but the visible search input displays missing-order-qa.
reproSteps: Open Site administration → User Accounts.
Search a fresh prefix with matching records and confirm the results.
Submit another query with no matches.
Use Browser Back and observe the earlier matching results while the visible search input retains the newer query.
Reload the restored URL and confirm the input and results agree.

relatedReference.distinction: This entry covers admin Users search; the related entry covers admin Repositories search.

matchingGuidance.scope: Covers a visible retained newer query alongside correctly restored earlier results after Browser Back. Subsequent actions submitting the retained query are separate effects.

reviewEvidence.basis: Explicit user acceptance at severity 1 based on Mo’s Users report; no independent Users reproduction established.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Contradictory visible search state; no incorrect saved records or data loss established.
analysis: Mo reports prior matching user rows returning while the newer unmatched query remains visible.
User explicitly accepted both admin entry points after clarification of the available evidence.

bugs.name: Setting a queue's maximum workers to 0 says 'Settings Updated' but it still runs a worker
bugs.summary: In Site Administration > Monitor > Queues, setting a queue's Max Number of Workers to 0 (or -1) is accepted with "Settings Updated", but the queue still starts a worker when work arrives, and nothing explains that 0 doesn't stop it. The setting looks like it caps workers at zero but has no such effect.
bugs.expected: A maximum of 0 either stops the queue's workers, or the form explains what 0 and -1 mean (or rejects them) instead of reporting success for a cap that isn't applied.
bugs.actual: After setting the repo-archive queue's maximum workers to 0 and saving ("Settings Updated"), downloading a repository ZIP started a worker: the queue showed 1 worker while the maximum still read 0, with no explanation.
reproSteps: In Site Administration > Monitor > Queues, open the repo-archive queue.
Set Max Number of Workers to 0 (or -1) and click Update Settings.
Download a repository as ZIP.
Reopen the queue's details and compare the number of workers with the maximum.

relatedReference.name: Queue worker cap below -1 is silently saved as -1
relatedReference.distinction: Same queue settings form, but that entry is a cap below -1 being silently changed to -1; this entry is a cap of 0 or -1 being accepted while a worker still runs.

bugs.name: Admin User Emails search drops the selected sort
bugs.summary: In Site Administration > User Emails, choosing a sort (such as reverse username) and then searching returns results in the default ascending email order and drops the sort from the URL.
bugs.expected: Searching User Emails keeps the selected sort order.
bugs.actual: With reverse username sort selected, searching showed the same results in ascending email order and the sort parameter disappeared.
reproSteps: Open Site Administration > User Emails and choose a non-default sort, such as reverse username.
Enter a search term and submit.
Check the order of the results and the selected sort.

relatedReference.name: Admin User Accounts search and filters drop the selected sort
relatedReference.distinction: Same missing sort field in the search form, but that entry is User Accounts; this entry is User Emails.

bugs.name: Clearing an organization's repository limit saves 0 instead of the default
bugs.summary: In an organization's settings, clearing Maximum Number of Repositories and saving stores a limit of 0, which blocks the organization from creating repositories, instead of falling back to the default (-1, use the global limit) when the field is unset.
bugs.expected: An empty repository limit falls back to the default of -1, the global setting.
bugs.actual: After clearing the field and saving, the organization's limit reopened as 0 and new repositories couldn't be created for it.
reproSteps: Open an organization's settings as a site administrator and note its Maximum Number of Repositories.
Clear the field and save.
Reopen the settings and check the saved limit, then try creating a repository in the organization.

bugs.name: Process cancellation dialog is clipped outside the mobile viewport
bugs.summary: After opening Cancel process at desktop width and resizing to 390 pixels, the dialog moves beyond the right and bottom edges. Dismissing with Escape and reopening at the mobile width still shows a clipped dialog with Confirm outside the viewport.
bugs.expected: The cancellation warning and both Cancel / Confirm buttons should fit within the mobile viewport.
bugs.actual: The dialog starts about 247 pixels from the left edge, with the right portion clipped. Only part of Cancel is visible and Confirm is offscreen; the whole-page AI assertion confirms this visible clipping.
reproSteps: As site administrator, open Monitoring → Trace → Stacktrace at desktop width.
Open Cancel Process on the monitoring request, without confirming.
Resize to 390 CSS pixels and inspect the dialog controls.
Dismiss with Escape and reopen at mobile width; observe Confirm offscreen and Cancel partially clipped.

relatedReference.distinction: The existing reference covers milestone deletion. This entry covers the process-cancellation confirmation in Site administration Monitoring; a shared root cause has not been established.

reviewEvidence.basis: Explicit user acceptance as a related severity-1 entry based on the Mo finding, with independent reviews not yet started.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Clipped dialog and offscreen confirmation controls at mobile width.
analysis: Mo reports clipping after desktop-to-mobile resize and after dismissing and reopening at mobile width.
No cancellation was confirmed in the reported test.
limitations: Independent browser and source verification pending.
A shared cause with milestone-dialog clipping is not established.

bugs.name: Create User Account button covers the user total on the mobile User Accounts page
bugs.summary: At a 390×844 viewport, Site Administration > User Accounts places the Create User Account button over the end of the 'User Account Management (Total: N)' heading, hiding the count.
bugs.expected: The heading and its total stay readable next to or above the Create User Account button at narrow widths.
bugs.actual: At 390×844 the button's left edge sat at about x=238 while the heading text ran to x=271, so the count was hidden under the button, including with a search that reduced the total to 1. At 480px and wider nothing is covered, and the button still opens the new user form.
reproSteps: Sign in as a site administrator and open Site Administration > User Accounts.
Set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Observe the Create User Account button covering the end of the heading and its total.
bugs.sourceCause: web_src/css/modules/header.css positions .ui.attached.header > .ui.right absolutely at the right edge without reserving space, so the heading text in templates/admin/user/list.tmpl runs underneath the button.

relatedReference.distinction: Same page and cause. That entry covers both the User Accounts and Repositories totals together; this entry is the User Accounts heading on its own.

bugs.name: Unadopted Repositories button covers the repository total on the mobile Repositories page
bugs.summary: At a 390×844 viewport, Site Administration > Repositories places the Unadopted Repositories button over the '(Total: N)' part of the 'Repository Management' heading, hiding the count.
bugs.expected: The heading and its total stay readable next to or above the Unadopted Repositories button at narrow widths.
bugs.actual: At 390×844 the button occupied about x=220–368 while '(Total: N)' ran from about x=185 to x=253, so the count was hidden, including with a search that reduced it to 'Total: 1'. At 480px and wider the heading is fully readable, and the button still opens Unadopted Repositories.
reproSteps: Sign in as a site administrator and open Site Administration > Repositories.
Set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Observe the Unadopted Repositories button covering the heading's total.
bugs.sourceCause: web_src/css/modules/header.css positions .ui.attached.header > .ui.right absolutely at the right edge without reserving space, so the heading text in templates/admin/repo/list.tmpl runs underneath the button.

relatedReference.distinction: Same page and cause. That entry covers both the User Accounts and Repositories totals together; this entry is the Repositories heading on its own.

bugs.name: Admin user details collapse into a narrow column with mid-word breaks on mobile
bugs.summary: At mobile widths, Site Administration's page for a user with a short email keeps User Details beside User Emails, leaving the details column about 100–140px wide, so every value breaks mid-word and the panel grows very tall. With a long email, the columns stack but the Primary and Activated badges are clipped.
bugs.expected: At narrow widths, the User Details and User Emails panels stack at full width with readable values and complete badges.
bugs.actual: For a fresh user with a short email at 375–414px, User Details was 103–142px wide beside User Emails, values broke mid-word ('Authe/ntic/ation', 'Restr/icted/:') and the panel was about 650–1100px tall. A fresh user with a long email stacked the columns, but the Primary badge showed as 'Primar'. The seeded users stack normally, and desktop widths show two equal columns.
reproSteps: Sign in as a site administrator and create a user with a short email address.
Set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Open Site Administration > User Accounts and open that user.
Observe the narrow User Details column with values broken mid-word.
bugs.sourceCause: web_src/css/admin.css .admin-responsive-columns wraps only when the columns' min-content widths overflow. The details column's min-content is nearly zero (flex-list.css min-width:0 and overflow-wrap:anywhere), while the email row keeps nowrap shrinkable .ui.label badges, so the columns stay side by side or the badges clip.

bugs.name: Monitoring Trace opens without showing traces or telling the administrator how to see them
bugs.summary: Site Administration > Monitoring > Trace opens a page that shows no trace: only a goroutine count over an empty panel, two unselected tabs and a Download diagnosis report button. Nothing says that stack traces appear only after choosing Running Processes or Stacktrace, so the page named Trace reads as just a diagnosis-report download.
bugs.expected: The Trace page shows traces, or clearly tells the administrator to choose Running Processes or Stacktrace to see them.
bugs.actual: The sidebar's Trace link opened /-/admin/monitor/stacktrace with neither tab selected, a '55 Goroutines' panel header with nothing under it, and no hint that the tabs load the traces. Choosing Running Processes loaded 28 processes with their stack traces.
reproSteps: Sign in as a site administrator.
Open Site Administration > Monitoring > Trace.
Observe that no trace is shown, no tab is selected, and nothing explains how to see traces.
bugs.sourceCause: routers/web/admin/stacktrace.go loads no process data unless a show parameter is set (deliberately, so the page can't fail), and templates/admin/stacktrace.tmpl renders the count header without any list or prompt, while templates/admin/trace_tabs.tmpl marks neither tab active.

matchingGuidance.scope: Reports that the Trace page doesn't show traces or doesn't explain how to reach them, or that its name doesn't match what it shows, match this entry.

relatedReference.distinction: That rejection is the claim that the empty default list is itself broken; this entry is the page not communicating how to see traces.

bugs.name: Diagnosis report silently turns a duration below 1 second into a 1-second report
bugs.summary: On Monitoring > Stacktrace, entering a diagnosis-report duration below the 1-second minimum (0, a negative number, an empty value or non-numeric text) gives no error or notice. The report is quietly collected for 1 second, producing a nearly empty CPU profile.
bugs.expected: A duration below the minimum, or one that isn't a number, is rejected with a message stating the allowed range, or the user is told it was raised to 1 second.
bugs.actual: seconds=0, an empty value and abc each returned a zip after about 1 second with a CPU profile of a few hundred bytes, with no message. The field shows no allowed range.
reproSteps: Sign in as a site administrator and open Site Administration > Monitoring > Stacktrace.
Replace the 10 in the Download diagnosis report field with 0 (or abc, or clear it).
Click Download diagnosis report.
Observe that the report downloads after about 1 second with no message about the invalid duration.
bugs.sourceCause: routers/web/admin/diagnosis.go MonitorDiagnosis reads ctx.FormInt64("seconds"), which returns 0 for empty or non-numeric input, then clamps with if seconds <= 1 { seconds = 1 } (and caps at 300) without reporting it. templates/admin/trace_tabs.tmpl renders the field as a plain text input (maxlength 3, default 10) with no range, hint or validation. The 1-second floor itself is intended (go-gitea/gitea#32973 lowered it from 5); the defect is that out-of-range input is coerced silently.

bugs.name: Performance Trace page is still served in production although its tab is hidden
bugs.summary: In production mode Gitea hides the Performance Trace tab from Monitoring > Trace on purpose, but the page itself isn't hidden: /-/admin/monitor/perftrace still renders the full trace records (HTTP and SQL timings) when opened by URL. Because the tab doesn't exist, the page shows the trace tab bar with no active tab and nothing in the admin UI links to it.
bugs.expected: When the Performance Trace tab is hidden (production mode), the page is hidden too, for example by returning 404 or redirecting to Stacktrace. Where the page is available, its tab is shown and highlighted.
bugs.actual: The tab bar on Monitoring > Trace showed only Running Processes and Stacktrace. Opening /-/admin/monitor/perftrace directly rendered about 100 trace records with neither tab highlighted, and no admin page linked to it.
reproSteps: Sign in as a site administrator on a production-mode instance and open Site Administration > Monitoring > Trace.
Observe that the tab bar has only Running Processes and Stacktrace.
Open /-/admin/monitor/perftrace directly.
Observe that the performance trace records render and no tab is active.
bugs.sourceCause: routers/web/admin/stacktrace.go monitorTraceCommon sets ShowAdminPerformanceTraceTab = !setting.IsProd, with a maintainer comment that the tab is hidden in production so end users don't see it and use 'download diagnosis report' instead; templates/admin/trace_tabs.tmpl renders the tab only when that flag is set. But routers/web/web.go registers /-/admin/monitor/perftrace unconditionally and routers/web/admin/perftrace.go PerfTrace never checks the flag or setting.IsProd, so the hidden page is still served, with PageIsAdminMonitorPerfTrace marking a tab that isn't rendered.

matchingGuidance.scope: A report that the Performance Trace page has no navigation entry or tab, is reachable only by typing its URL, or opens with no active tab counts toward this entry. Hiding the tab in production is intended; the accepted defect is that the page behind the hidden tab is still served.
